newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion ends mixed on limited activity.
newsitem.headline: India bullion ends mixed on limited activity.

text.p: Silver (.999) closed 50 rupees higher at 6,380 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,330 rupees on the back of speculative buying influenced by a rally in the world market, dealers said.
Silver was up by 30 rupees per kg on Thursday.
"In the early trade silver opened higher at 6,400 rupees but later on slow industrial buying and light profit-taking trimmed some of the early gains towards the close," one broker added.
"Fresh arrivals of the imported silver also subdued the market sentiment after a firm start," he added.

Gold 24 carat closed steady at 4,530 rupees per 10 gramme amid lower than expected seasonal buying while limited supplies kept offerings at a low ebb. Gold was up by 10 rupees per 10 gramme on Thursday.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.64 gramme) closed steady at 53,000 rupees per piece after gaining 100 rupees on Thursday.

Narrow fluctuations of gold prices in the world market also kept local prices in a narrow price range, but sentiment at the close was slightly firm as marketmen were expecting improved festival buying next week.
